facts.title: Lyria 3 Pro adds up to three-minute tracks and more song-structure control
facts.summary: Google said Lyria 3 Pro allows creation of tracks up to three minutes long and better prompting for intros, verses, choruses, and bridges. Google also said the model is rolling into Gemini, Google Vids, Vertex AI, AI Studio, and ProducerAI.

facts.title: Suno says it reached 2M paid subscribers and $300M ARR
facts.summary: Music Business Worldwide reported Suno CEO Mikey Shulman said Suno had reached 2 million paid subscribers, $300 million ARR, and 100 million total users. This remains a company claim rather than an audited disclosure, but it is strategically important if directionally true.

facts.title: Global recorded music revenues reached $31.7B in 2025; paid subscriptions hit 837M
facts.summary: IFPI reported recorded music revenues grew 6.4% in 2025 to $31.7 billion. Paid subscription streaming grew 8.8%, and paid streaming subscription accounts reached 837 million globally.

facts.title: Music publishers pressed the Anthropic lyrics case around fair use and market substitution
facts.summary: Reuters reported UMG, Concord, and ABKCO asked a California judge to reject Anthropic's fair-use defense, arguing Claude can reproduce lyrics on demand and that its lyric outputs compete with and dilute the market for the originals.

facts.title: U.S. courts are beginning to draw lines around lawful sourcing, piracy risk, and market harm in AI training cases
facts.summary: Reuters' legal analysis said 2025 decisions created early guideposts: courts were receptive to fair-use arguments for lawfully acquired training data, but piracy and improper sourcing remain major risk points and market-harm analysis still matters.

facts.title: Survey of 1,525 musicians shows AI usage is higher among pros than hobbyists, but practical use is led by workflow tools
facts.summary: In the survey, 67% of respondents said they had used AI for music-related work; 78% of professionals reported using AI versus 60% of hobbyists. Among AI users, stem separation led at 71% adoption, while full-song generation was 24%. 58% worried about authenticity and 55% about copyright and licensing.

facts.title: Spotify is beta testing artist profile approval controls to reduce misattribution and AI slop
facts.summary: TechCrunch reported Spotify's new Artist Profile Protection beta lets artists review and approve or decline releases delivered under their names before they go live on artist pages. Spotify framed artist identity protection as a top priority for 2026.

facts.title: Deezer licensed its AI-detection technology to Sacem and said it removed up to 85% of fraudulent AI streams from its royalty pool in 2025
facts.summary: Reuters reported Deezer licensed its AI-music detection tool to Sacem, said it flagged over 13.4 million AI tracks, and said it now receives around 60,000 fully AI-created tracks per day, roughly 39% of total daily uploads.

facts.title: UNESCO projects generative-AI-driven revenue losses of 24% for music creators by 2028
facts.summary: UNESCO said generative AI outputs are projected to cause global revenue losses of 24% for music creators by 2028. The same report also highlighted market concentration and opaque curation systems as structural risks for lesser-known creators.

creator_workflow: The best-supported near-term wedge in music AI is workflow assistance inside existing creation behavior, not wholesale replacement of musicians.
That keeps Musio's best opportunity closer to controllable musical utility than to generic finished-song generation.
licensing_and_policy: The legal and policy environment is still unsettled, but the direction of travel is clear enough to matter: lawful sourcing, transparency, and rights posture are strategic assets.
The Anthropic lyrics dispute matters because music-specific cases emphasize output substitution and on-demand reproduction, not just abstract training doctrine.
market_structure: The market is simultaneously bigger and messier: industry revenues are growing, but oversupply, fraud, and platform concentration are increasing pressure on trust and discovery.
Products associated with quality, control, and workflow fit should benefit more than products adding undifferentiated volume.
competitive_landscape: Google's distribution and Suno's claimed scale make the category look commercially real, but they also make the generic AI-music-app lane harder to win independently.
Musio's more defensible angle remains the layer between musical intent and usable, commercially credible output.
distribution_controls: Spotify's identity-protection beta and Deezer's AI-detection licensing point the same direction: distribution platforms increasingly need anti-spam, anti-impersonation, and provenance controls.
That strengthens the case for Musio to position around trustworthiness and commercial cleanliness rather than raw output volume.

Potentially an attractive acquisition candidate if it becomes a differentiated sound/workflow layer for serious music creation and media production.
